slides.title: 17.2.2 Pruning Impossible Solutions
keyPoints: Pruning rejects partial choices that cannot be extended to a legal solution under the current constraints.
A column conflict already violates the final requirement, so exploring descendants cannot repair it.
Rejecting that branch is therefore safe.
A heuristic such as “this column looks unlikely” would need a different justification before it could discard.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 17, treat 17.2.2 Pruning Impossible Solutions as an algorithmic claim. Pruning rejects partial choices that cannot be extended to a legal solution under the current constraints. A column conflict already violates the final requirement, so exploring descendants cannot repair it. Rejecting that branch is therefore safe. A heuristic such as “this column looks unlikely” would need a different justification before it could discard solutions. The search can still be exponential despite constant-time conflict checks. There are n choices at each row before constraints, and no repeated columns limits complete assignments to at most n! candidates. Early diagonal pruning reduces actual work but does not turn the general search into a polynomial-time method. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. First reproduce the known counts already in the companion, including the empty board and the unsatisfiable two- and three-row boards. Add a version that stores the column chosen in each row for a four-row board.
